data.title: Sidebar
data.tagline: Keep navigation in a vertical column beside the content
data.description: A sidebar suits products with many sections, grouped tools, or workspaces that users switch between often. Give the content enough room and provide a compact or temporary version on smaller screens. Do not make every nested level visible at once.

use: Navigation that needs labels and icons
avoid: Use a wide permanent sidebar on a narrow screen
Expand every nested group by default
Mix page navigation with unrelated content
Leave too little width for the main task

lessonPractice.title: An admin app has more than ten grouped areas such as projects, members, billing, and permissions. Users switch often and need a large workspace. How should it lay out?

options.label: Use grouped sidebar navigation, let content flex, and turn the sidebar into a dismissible drawer on narrow screens
options.feedback: A stable sidebar fits frequent hierarchical access, while flexible content and a mobile drawer preserve working width.

options.label: Put every entry in one top bar and allow horizontal scrolling when it no longer fits
options.feedback: Many grouped destinations lose hierarchy and overview, while horizontal scrolling makes locations unpredictable.

options.label: Keep the same permanent sidebar width on desktop and mobile and give content the remainder
options.feedback: Mobile content loses the width required for primary tasks, so navigation should become an on-demand layer.

data.agentPrompt: Use a left-sidebar layout for the admin app with Projects, Team, Billing, and System groups and a flexing workspace. Allow collapse on desktop, use a modal drawer on mobile, and verify focus and active-menu state.
